justification: One setting in frontend-nextjs/vercel.json moves every API function to Sydney, which is where the database is. It is Minor in lines but project-wide in effect, so the measurement below is on one route and the risks are listed.

pre_impl.existing_data: No regions key was set, so Vercel used its default of US East. The database host is aws-1-ap-southeast-2 and most outside calls go to NSW government services.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A function that calls a service hosted in the US would get slower. Of the hosts the API routes call, the large majority are NSW government services and our own domain; the Python backend's region is not measured here.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to the next deploy of every function. No data is written and no route code changes.

break_it.scenario: The Python backend or another service is hosted in the US, so a function now makes a longer hop than before.
break_it.what_happens: Routes that depend on it get slower, and a route with a long timeout could take longer end to end.
break_it.how: Not mitigated in this change. It is reversible by removing one line, and the routes' maxDuration limits are unchanged.
break_it.repro: Time a route that calls the Python backend before and after the deploy, for example one that reads PYTHON_API_URL.

residual_risk: Measured on the brief route only: p95 3.31 s in the default region against 0.24 s in Sydney, 108 calls each, paced under the 30 a minute limit. Other routes are expected to improve for the same reason but were not measured. The Python backend region is unknown. Revert is one line.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: time one route that calls the Python backend before and after
